newsitem.title: ITALY: U.S. official at summit confirms force decision.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official at summit confirms force decision.

text.p: A U.S. official at the World Food Summit in Rome confirmed on Wednesday that Washington intended to announce an agreement in principle to take part in a multinational force for eastern Zaire.

"That is currently under very extensive discussion at the highest levels of government today and I think an announcement will shortly be made about our intention to join the international force," U.S. undersecretary of state for global affairs Tim Wirth told a news conference.

Wirth, who is a member of the U.S. delegation to the Rome summit, praised an offer by Canada to command such a force to help bring assistance to over one million starving Hutu refugees caught in the crossfire of four weeks of fighting.
"The Canadian offer is deeply appreciated," Wirth said in response to a question about a possible U.S. role.
The United States has been under mounting pressure to join in a multinational effort, especially from France and Canada.
President Bill Clinton discussed Zaire's refugee crisis with other world leaders by telephone on Wednesday and a White House announcement was expected later, officials in Washington said.
